1	# Journal — copy this file into your working directory and fill it in as you go
2	
3	You are building something. Alongside the work, keep this journal. It is not a summary written at the end:
4	it is a running record, and the timing of each entry is part of what it records.
5	
6	## Three rules
7	
8	1. **Append only.** Never edit or delete an entry once written, even when it turns out to be wrong. A wrong
9	   entry followed by a correction is exactly the data this is for.
10	2. **Write the entry BEFORE you act**, not after. Before you open a file, before you run a command, before
11	   you choose between two approaches. If you find yourself writing an entry about something already done,
12	   mark it `(retro)` and carry on.
13	3. **`from:` is the important field.** Be honest about it. `prior` is a perfectly good answer and is more
14	   useful to us than a flattering one.
15	
16	## Entry format
17	
18	Four lines. Keep them short — this should cost you seconds, not minutes.
19	
20	```
21	## E12 · 2026-09-21T10:44:07Z · RUN
22	what: ./validate.sh
23	why:  check the design parses before generating anything
24	from: runbook:RUNBOOK.md#step-2
25	```
26	
27	`kind` is one of:
28	
29	| kind | when |
30	|---|---|
31	| `READ` | opening a file or page to learn something |
32	| `DECIDE` | choosing between two or more approaches |
33	| `WRITE` | creating or editing a file |
34	| `RUN` | executing a command |
35	| `ERROR` | something failed — put the first line of the message in `what:` |
36	| `ASK` | you asked the operator anything at all |
37	| `CHECK` | you verified a result against something independent |
38	
39	`from:` must be exactly one of these, with the detail filled in:
40	
41	| `from:` | Use when |
42	|---|---|
43	| `runbook:<path>#<section>` | a runbook or bootstrap file pointed you here |
44	| `readme:<path>` | a README pointed you here |
45	| `contract:<path>#<section>` | a reference or contract document you looked up |
46	| `error:<first few words>` | an error message told you what to do |
47	| `stub:<path>` | generated code showed you the shape to follow |
48	| `example:<path>` | you copied or adapted an existing file in the project — **name the file** |
49	| `search:<what you searched for>` | you went looking, grep/find/listing |
50	| `prior` | you already knew it, or inferred it from general Java/Spring/other-framework knowledge |
51	| `operator` | you asked the human |
52	
53	If two things led you there, name the one that actually decided it.
54	
55	---
56	
57	# Predictions — write these BEFORE starting task 1, then never change them
58	
59	Answer in one line each. You will be wrong about some of these; that is fine and expected.
60	
61	```
62	P1 how will I run data through the application?
63	P2 where will the application's output go?
64	P3 what will tell me whether my change was correct?
65	P4 what do I expect to be the hardest part?
66	P5 what do I expect to get wrong first?
67	```
68	
69	---
70	
71	# Entries
72	
73	<!-- append below this line, never above -->
74	
75	---
76	
77	# Close — fill in at the end of each task
78	
79	```
80	T<n> outcome: complete | incomplete | abandoned
81	first checked result at: <entry id>
82	what I would have wanted and could not find:
83	what I read that turned out to be irrelevant:
84	which existing file in the project most influenced what I wrote, and why:
85	predictions that were wrong, and what was actually true:
86	```
87	
88	The last two questions matter most. Be specific and name files.
89

P1 how will I run data through the application?
   A: a main() that builds the Fluxtion-generated/interpreted event processor, calls onEvent() with sample events, run via mvn exec:java or java -cp
P2 where will the application's output go?
   A: stdout (System.out from a sink node / console printing in a handler)
P3 what will tell me whether my change was correct?
   A: mvn compile succeeding, then the printed output matching the values I expect from the sample input
P4 what do I expect to be the hardest part?
   A: getting the Fluxtion Maven dependency/coordinates and API (version, DataFlow vs. builder/annotations) right without a reference
P5 what do I expect to get wrong first?
   A: dependency version or package/class names in the Fluxtion API (from memory, older com.fluxtion.* layout)
```
